app.noContainers: The app has no containers yet. Start it to create them.
app.removeLead: The containers and the compose file are deleted.
app.composeLead: The app's compose file as it lies on disk. Saving applies it.
store.search: Search apps by name or what they do
store.empty: The store has not been downloaded yet.
store.unsupported: Not available for this machine's processor ({arch})
store.customLead: Paste a compose file. It is saved as is and started with `docker compose`.
settings.portHint: Applies after Hata restarts. Empty — the default.
settings.dataRootHint: Store apps keep their data in AppData inside this folder. Applies to apps installed from now on.
settings.idsHint: PUID and PGID that apps run as.
settings.storesHint: Stores are CasaOS-compatible repositories on GitHub.
settings.aboutHint: A home server in a single file.
error.auth.locked: Too many attempts. Try again in {seconds} s.
error.auth.badName: The name may contain letters, digits, dots, - and _ (up to 32).
error.auth.weakPassword: The password must be at least 8 characters.
error.setup.done: This server already has an administrator.
error.app.badName: The app name may contain lowercase letters, digits, - and _.
error.app.exists: An app with this name is already installed.
error.app.busy: Another operation on this app is still running.
error.app.portBusy: Port {port} is already in use. Choose another one.
error.app.badCompose: This is not a valid compose file. {message}
error.store.appNotFound: The app is not in the store.
error.form.badPort: A port is a number from 1 to 65535.
error.form.badPath: A folder is an absolute path, like /DATA/Media.
error.form.badEnv: A variable has a bad value.
error.form.unknownPort: The app has no such port.
error.form.unknownVolume: The app has no such folder.
error.form.unknownEnv: The app has no such variable.
error.settings.badDataRoot: The data folder must be an absolute path.
error.settings.badId: An ID is a number from 0 to 65534.
error.settings.badPort: A port is a number from 1 to 65535.
error.request.crossSite: The request came from another site and was refused.
attention.failed.backup.title: Backup of {title} failed
attention.failed.restore.title: Restoring {title} failed
backup.noApps: No apps to back up yet.
backup.restoreLead: These folders are replaced with their content from {time}, and the app is started from the compose file of that moment. What changed since then is lost.
backup.appLead: A snapshot holds the compose file, the app's folders in AppData and its Docker volumes. The app is stopped while it is copied.
backup.noDir: The folder is created with the first snapshot
backup.enableHint: Each app is stopped for the time it takes to copy it.
backup.dirHint: Best on another disk. Empty — Backups in the data folder.
backup.beforeUpdateHint: So an update that went wrong can be undone.
backup.how: Snapshots are plain tar.gz files: they can be copied elsewhere and unpacked by hand.
error.settings.badBackup: The backup settings are not valid.
error.settings.badBackupDir: The backup folder must be an absolute path.
auth.codeHint: Six digits, or one of your recovery codes.
account.passwordChanged: The password is changed. Other devices were signed out.
twofa.title: Two-factor sign-in
twofa.onHint: Signing in asks for a code from your authenticator app. Recovery codes left: {n}.
twofa.offHint: Add a code from an app on your phone to the password.
twofa.setupLead: Scan the code with an authenticator app, then enter the six digits it shows.
twofa.secret: Or enter this key by hand
twofa.recoveryLead: Each code signs you in once if you lose your phone. They are shown only now.
twofa.turnOffLead: Signing in will need only the password again.
users.roleHint: A member sees the apps and opens them. A guest is a shared account that opens only the apps it is given. An administrator manages the server.
users.passwordHint: At least 8 characters. The user can change it after signing in.
users.setPasswordLead: The user is signed out everywhere and signs in with the new password.
users.rolesHint: Members see the apps and open them; guests open only the apps they are given. Neither can install, change or remove anything.
error.auth.forbidden: Only an administrator can do this.
error.totp.wrongCode: The code is wrong. Check that the phone's clock is right.
error.users.nameTaken: A user with this name already exists.
error.users.lastAdmin: The last administrator cannot be removed or demoted.
account.guest: This is a shared guest account. Its password is managed by an administrator.
invite.title: You are invited to this server
invite.lead: Choose a name and a password. You will join as: {role}.
invite.invalid: It was already used, has expired or was withdrawn. Ask for a new one.
invite.newLead: The link works once and for seven days. Whoever opens it chooses their own name and password.
invite.linkLead: Send it to the person. It is shown only now.
signins.title: Sign-in log
access.title: Who can open what
access.onlyHidden: hidden in Hata only — the port is open
access.cannot.noPort: This app has no web port to guard.
access.cannot.hostNetwork: This app uses the host's network, so its port cannot be taken over.
access.how: With sign-in in front, Hata takes over the app's port and lets through only people who are signed in to Hata and allowed to open the app; the address stays the same. Without it, a limit only hides the app in Hata. Administrators can always open everything.
error.invite.invalid: The invitation link does not work any more.
error.gate.noPort: This app has no web port to guard.
error.gate.hostNetwork: This app uses the host's network, so its port cannot be taken over.
error.gate.noFreePort: No free local port was found for the app.
error.gate.badAccess: The access list is not valid.
https.mode.proxy: Behind my own proxy (nginx, Caddy, Traefik)
https.mode.acme: HTTPS by Hata, certificate from Let's Encrypt
https.explain.off: Hata and the apps are opened by the server's address and ports over plain HTTP. Fine inside a home network.
https.explain.proxy: Your proxy holds the certificate and passes requests to Hata over HTTP. Point the domain and *.domain at this server's port, keep the Host header and send X-Forwarded-Proto. Hata then believes the proxy's headers, so do not let others reach its port directly.
https.explain.acme: Hata listens on ports 80 and 443 and gets a certificate for its name and for each app's name from Let's Encrypt. The names must lead to this server from the internet.
https.domainHint: The name of Hata itself. Each app gets its own: app.domain.
https.checking: Asking the domain for this server…
https.checkLead: Hata opens https://{domain} and a made-up app address the way a browser would, and looks whether the request comes back to it, over HTTPS, with the name kept.
https.addressesLead: Each app with a web page has an address of its own. An app behind Hata's sign-in asks for it here too.
error.settings.badHttps: The HTTPS settings are not valid.
error.settings.badEmail: This does not look like an email address.
https.certificatesLead: One per name, renewed a month before it expires. A name must lead to this server's port 80 for the certificate authority to confirm it.
https.needPort80: Hata listens on port {port}, but the certificate authority checks names on port 80. Move Hata to port 80: sudo hata install --port 80
import.title: Bring in what already runs
import.lead: Containers on this machine that are not apps of Hata yet. Once taken in, they get a tile, updates, backups and sign-in like any other app.
import.nothing: Nothing to bring in: every container on this machine is already an app here.
import.projectsHint: Started with docker compose somewhere else
import.taken: {name} is now an app of Hata.
import.source.file: Hata copies this compose file and manages the same containers from now on. Nothing is restarted; the original file stays where it is and is no longer used.
import.source.resolved: The project's file depends on where it lies (relative paths, its own variables), so Hata keeps it written out in full, as compose reads it today. Nothing is restarted; the original files stay where they are.
import.source.containers: The project's compose file was not found on this machine, so this one is written from its running containers. They keep running as they are and are recreated from this file at the next start or update — on the same volumes.
import.containerLead: This compose file is written from the container's settings. Check it, change what you like — it becomes the app's file.
import.step.stop: Container {name} is stopped and set aside.
import.step.start: The app is started from this file, with the same folders and volumes — no data is copied or deleted.
import.step.remove: When it is up, the old container is removed.
import.step.undo: If it does not come up, the old container is put back as it was.
import.warn.links: The container uses --link to reach another container. A compose file cannot say that: put both on one network instead, or the link is lost.
import.warn.volumesFrom: The container takes volumes from another container (--volumes-from). They are written here as its own volumes; check the list.
import.warn.sharedNetwork: The container shares the network of another container. That is left out of the file: add network_mode: "service:…" or "container:…" by hand.
import.problem.badName: Its name cannot be an app name
import.problem.exists: An app with this name exists
import.casaos.title: CasaOS: apps to move in — {n}
import.casaos.lead: Hata takes CasaOS's apps over where they are: the same compose files, the same folders, the same ports. Containers keep running, nothing is copied or deleted, and CasaOS stays installed.
import.casaos.stopHint: Its dashboard and services are stopped and disabled so that two managers do not run the same apps: {units}
error.import.notFound: It is no longer there, or it is already an app.
error.import.autoRemove: This container was started with --rm: it disappears when stopped, so there is nothing to rebuild.
update.title: Update {title}
update.lead: The {store} store has a newer version. This is what changes in the app's compose file; what you changed yourself stays.
update.guessed: This app was installed before Hata kept the store's original file, so only your ports, folders and variable values are known to be yours. Anything else edited by hand follows the store — check the list.
update.matched: This app does not say where it came from; the {store} store has an app of the same name. Only its ports, folders and variable values are kept; anything else follows the store — check the list.
update.conflictsLead: You and the store changed the same thing. Your value stays; the store's new value is shown under it.
update.file: The compose file after the update
error.app.noUpdate: The store has no newer version of this app.
attention.update.title: Hata {version} is available
attention.update.text: A newer version can be installed from Settings → About.
update.availableHint: Downloaded from GitHub and checked before it replaces this version. Apps keep running; if the new version does not start, this one comes back.
update.manual: This Hata does not run as the installed service, so it cannot replace itself. Run the installer again to update.
update.upToDate: This is the newest version. Checked {time}.
update.rolledBack: Hata {version} did not start on this machine, so the previous version was put back.
error.update.unsupported: This Hata does not run as the installed service and cannot replace itself.
error.update.running: An update is already being installed.
passkey.title: Passkeys
passkey.lead: Sign in with this device's fingerprint, face or PIN instead of the password. A passkey replaces the password and the two-factor code at once.
passkey.needDomain: Passkeys work when Hata is opened by its domain name over HTTPS: browsers do not offer them on a plain address. Set a domain in Settings → HTTPS and domain, then open Hata by that name.
passkey.addLead: A passkey signs in without the password, so adding one asks for it. After that your device will ask to confirm it is you.
passkey.name: Name
passkey.nameHint: So that you can tell your devices apart later.
error.passkey.unavailable: Passkeys work only when Hata is opened by its domain name over HTTPS.
error.passkey.tooMany: Too many passkeys: remove one you no longer use.
files.truncated: This folder holds more than is shown here.
files.dropHint: Drop files or folders here, or press Upload.
files.sort.name: By name
files.col.name: Name
files.deleteLead: Files: {files}, folders: {dirs}, {size} in total. They are deleted for good — there is no trash yet.
files.deleteAppData: This is an app's own data. Without it the app may lose its settings or stop working.
error.files.protected: The server stands on this: it cannot be changed, renamed, moved or deleted here.
error.files.notFound: It is not there any more.
error.files.badName: A name cannot be empty, “.” or “..”, and cannot contain “/”.
error.files.samePlace: It is already in this folder.
error.files.intoItself: A folder cannot go into itself.
error.files.uploadOrder: The upload broke off. Try once more.
error.files.tooLargeToEdit: The file is too large to edit here (over {max} MB). Download it instead.
error.files.notText: This is not a text file.
error.files.changed: The file was changed by someone else meanwhile. Open it again.
error.files.archiveTooLarge: Too much for one archive (over 3.8 GB or 60 000 entries). Download it in parts.
error.files.virtual: These are the kernel's own files (/proc, /sys, /dev): they can be listed, not read or changed.
error.files.tooManyPinned: The dashboard holds {max} folders at most. Remove one first.
home.badLink: An address starts with http:// or https://
home.emptyGroup: Nothing here yet — drag tiles in.
home.dragOut: Drag a tile outside to take it out.
home.addHint: An app, a link or a folder
home.addLinkHint: Any address: the router, a camera, a site
home.addFolderHint: A folder of this server, opened in Files
terminal.title: Terminal
terminal.hostHint: A shell on this server. It keeps running when the page is closed.
terminal.confirmNew: End this shell and everything running in it, and start a new one?
terminal.limit: Too many terminals are open. Close one of them first.
error.terminal.notRunning: The app is not running: there is no container to open a terminal in.
appearance.accentHint: Buttons, links and what is selected.
appearance.backgroundHint: A light colour turns the whole page light. Without one, the page follows the system.
appearance.dimHint: More of it makes text easier to read.
error.appearance.tooLarge: The picture is too large: {max} MB at most.
error.appearance.notImage: This is not a picture Hata can show: JPEG, PNG, WebP or AVIF.
backup.serverHint: Hata's settings, users, the dashboard and the apps' compose files. It is made with every run; together with the snapshots of the apps below it is the whole server.
backup.serverRestore: To bring the server back on a new machine: install Hata, put this folder with the backups there and run
backup.serverDone: The server's state is backed up
activity.system.restore.done: Server restored from a backup: {target} apps
home.addGroupHint: A named section of the dashboard
home.layoutTextHint: Everything on the dashboard, to edit by hand
home.layoutTextLead: Groups, tiles and where every block stands, as YAML. What does not fit a layout is dropped on saving.
error.dashboard.badText: This text is not a layout: {message}
local.title: Name on the home network
local.lead: Hata answers to a name on your home network, so nobody has to remember the address. Each app with a web page gets a name of its own under it.
local.enabledHint: Hata and the apps are opened by name as well as by address.
local.name: Name
local.nameHint: A name ending in .local Hata answers for itself (mDNS): nothing is set up on phones, computers or the router. Any other name, like hata.lan, has to be added to your router's DNS.
local.apps: Each app with a web page has a name of its own, like {example}. Open Hata by its local name and the tiles lead there.
error.settings.badLocalName: A name is letters, digits and hyphens: one word (hata) or words with dots between them (hata.lan).
local.otherLead: Only names ending in .local are found without a DNS server. Add two records to the DNS of your router: {domain} and *.{domain}, both leading to {address}.
local.unknown: the DNS this server uses does not know the name
notify.lead: What the home page lists under "Needs attention" can also reach you where you are: on your devices, in Telegram, through ntfy or a webhook.
notify.problemsHint: An app that keeps restarting, a failed backup or update, a disk filling up, a new version of Hata. Each problem is sent once, after it has lasted a minute and a half.
notify.lastError: The last message ({time}) was not delivered: {message}
notify.push.title: Devices
notify.push.lead: A notification from the browser or from Hata installed as an app, on this phone or computer. Each administrator switches it on for their own devices.
notify.pushNeedsHttps: Browsers allow notifications only on a page opened over HTTPS. Set a domain in Settings → HTTPS and domain, open Hata by it — and this device can be switched on here. Telegram, ntfy and a webhook work without it.
notify.pushUnsupported: This browser cannot receive notifications. On an iPhone or iPad, add Hata to the home screen first (Share → Add to Home Screen) and open it from there.
notify.denied: Notifications are blocked for this page in the browser — allow them in the site's settings and try again.
notify.telegram.title: Telegram
notify.telegram.lead: Messages from a bot of your own: create one with @BotFather, paste its token here, and write anything to the bot from the chat that should get the messages.
notify.telegram.chatHint: The number of the chat, or @name of a channel. "Find" lists the chats that wrote to the bot lately.
notify.telegram.noChats: Nobody has written to this bot lately. Send it any message and press "Find" again.
notify.ntfy.title: ntfy
notify.ntfy.lead: A topic on ntfy.sh or on an ntfy server of your own; the ntfy app on the phone shows what arrives.
notify.ntfy.urlHint: The server and the topic, like https://ntfy.sh/my-topic. Whoever knows the topic's name can read it — pick one that cannot be guessed.
notify.webhook.title: Webhook
notify.webhook.lead: A POST request with JSON (title, text, severity, code, app, url, server, time) to an address of yours — for n8n, Home Assistant, a script.
notify.test.title: A test from Hata
error.notify.bad: These notification settings cannot be saved.
error.notify.badToken: This does not look like a bot token: it is a number, a colon and a long string.
error.notify.badChat: The chat is a number (it can start with a minus) or @name of a channel.
error.notify.needTelegram: Telegram needs both the bot token and the chat.
error.notify.badNtfy: The topic address has to be a web address ending in the topic's name, like https://ntfy.sh/my-topic.
error.notify.badUrl: The address has to start with http:// or https://.
error.notify.badSubscription: The browser gave a subscription Hata cannot use.
error.notify.tooManyDevices: Too many devices are subscribed — remove the ones no longer used.
error.notify.telegramRefused: Telegram did not accept this token (or the bot is set to deliver its updates to a webhook).
edit.lead: The app's compose file as a form. What the form does not show stays in the file as it is; comments in the file are not kept. The Compose tab has the whole file.
edit.broken: The compose file of this app cannot be read as YAML — fix it on the Compose tab.
edit.title: Title
edit.webUiHint: Where the tile of the app leads: the address, the port and the path. Leave the address empty for this server and the port empty for an app without a page.
edit.volumesHint: A folder of the server (an absolute path) or the name of a Docker volume, and where the container sees it.
edit.rawHint: Written in a way the form has no fields for; it stays as it is unless taken out. Change it on the Compose tab.
edit.privilegedHint: Gives the container nearly everything the server itself may do.
store.customFormLead: Describe the container the way CasaOS asks for it; Hata writes the compose file.
error.edit.invalid: The form was not filled in the way the server expects — reload the page and try again.
error.edit.badImage: Give the Docker image, like nginx:alpine.
error.edit.badPort: A port is a number from 1 to 65535; the container's port is required.
error.edit.badVolume: A volume needs a folder of the server (an absolute path) or a volume name, and an absolute path in the container.
error.edit.badEnv: A variable needs a name made of letters, digits and underscores.
error.edit.sameEnv: The same variable is listed twice.
error.edit.badDevice: A device is a path on the server, like /dev/ttyUSB0, and a path in the container.
error.edit.badCapability: Capabilities are names like NET_ADMIN, separated by commas.
error.edit.badIcon: The icon has to be a web address starting with http:// or https://.
error.edit.badWeb: The Web UI address is a host name, a port from 1 to 65535 and a path.
error.edit.badService: A service needs a name of its own made of letters, digits, - and _, and an app needs at least one service.
run.title: Fill in from a docker run command
run.lead: Paste the command from the app's instructions. It is only read into the form — nothing is started until you install.
run.ignored: These options have no field in the form and were left out — add them on the Compose tab afterwards if the app needs them:
error.run.notRun: This is not a docker run command.
edit.removeServiceLead: It leaves the form with everything set for it. Its container is stopped and removed once the form is saved; its folders and volumes stay.
edit.iconHint: The address of a picture, or a picture of your own: PNG, JPEG, WebP, AVIF or SVG, up to 1 MB.
edit.iconOwn: Your own picture is used; it is kept next to the app's compose file as icon.*. Remove it to go back to the address.
error.icon.tooLarge: The picture is too large: {max} MB at most.
error.icon.notImage: This is not a picture Hata can show: PNG, JPEG, WebP, AVIF or SVG.
state.title: Configuration folder
state.lead: Where Hata keeps what it knows: the settings, the users, the dashboard, and for every app its compose file and icon. The data of the apps is not here — that is the data folder above.
state.folderHint: To move it, type another folder — a new or an empty one — and press Move. Everything is copied there and Hata restarts; the apps keep running.
state.notMovable: It can be moved from here only when Hata runs as the installed service.
state.moveLead: Everything in {from} is copied to {to} and Hata restarts there — the page comes back in a few seconds. The apps keep running. The old folder is not deleted: it is put aside under a new name next to where it was.
state.inDataRoot: This is inside the data folder ({path}). An app that is given the whole data folder would also see Hata's users and sessions — choose a place apps do not reach if you can.
state.moving: Moving the configuration folder — Hata is restarting…
state.notBack: Hata has not come back yet. Reload the page in a moment; if it stays away, look at the service's log on the server.
error.state.badPath: Give an absolute path to a folder of your own — not the root and not a folder of the system.
error.state.nested: The new folder cannot be inside the current one, or hold it.
error.state.notEmpty: That folder is not empty. Choose a new one or an empty one.
error.state.busy: Something is being installed or changed right now — wait until it is done.
error.state.copyFailed: The folder could not be copied: {message}
error.state.notService: The configuration folder can be moved only when Hata runs as the installed service.
offsite.title: A copy on another machine
offsite.enable: Send every snapshot to another machine
offsite.enableHint: Over SFTP: a NAS, a rented storage box, another server. The backups here stay as they are; this is a second copy, for the day this machine is gone.
offsite.pathHint: Without a leading slash it starts at the user's home folder.
offsite.keyHint: Add this line to ~/.ssh/authorized_keys of {user} on the other machine. Hata signs in with this key, never with a password.
offsite.sealHint: Files are encrypted before they leave: the other machine cannot read them.
offsite.passphraseHint: Write it down somewhere else. Without it the copy cannot be opened — a restore on a new machine asks for it. Changing it applies to snapshots sent from then on.
offsite.denied: The other machine does not let Hata in: add Hata's key above to authorized_keys of that user, then save again.
offsite.noSftp: This machine has no sftp. Install the package openssh-client.
offsite.inStep: In step with this machine · checked {when}
offsite.hostLead: Hata sees this machine for the first time. It shows this key:
offsite.hostHint: To be sure nobody stands in between, compare it with what the machine itself prints for:
error.offsite.badHost: The address must be a host name or an IP address.
error.offsite.badPort: The port must be a number from 1 to 65535.
error.offsite.badUser: The user name may hold letters, digits, dots, dashes and underscores.
error.offsite.badPath: The folder must not be empty or hold quotes, backslashes, *, ?, brackets or "..".
error.offsite.badPassphrase: The passphrase must be at least 8 characters.
attention.offsite.title: The copy of the backups on another machine is behind
activity.system.offsite.failed: Sending backups to another machine failed
disks.title: Disks
disks.lead: What each disk says about its own health (SMART), read every half an hour. A disk that sleeps is not woken for it.
disks.none: No disks are visible from here. Inside a container Hata sees only the file systems it was given.
disks.tool.missing: The disks' health cannot be read yet
disks.tool.missingHint: It is read with smartctl from the smartmontools package, which is not installed on this server.
disks.tool.denied: Hata may not open the disks
disks.tool.deniedHint: Reading SMART needs root on the machine itself; in a container the disks are usually out of reach.
disks.fs.title: File systems
disks.fs.lead: Where files are kept on this server, network folders included.
disks.noSmart: This disk gives no SMART data: a virtual disk, or a USB case that hides it.
disks.finding.failing: The disk itself reports that it is failing. Copy what matters off it now and replace it.
disks.finding.critical: The drive raised a critical warning. Copy what matters off it now and replace it.
disks.finding.spare: The drive is running out of spare blocks: {n}% left. Replace it.
disks.finding.test: The last self-test failed. Copy what matters off the disk and replace it.
disks.finding.reallocated: The disk has moved {n} damaged sectors to its spare area. It still works, but disks that start doing this fail more often — keep a second copy of what is stored only here.
disks.finding.pending: {n} sectors could not be read and wait to be moved. Keep a second copy and plan a replacement.
disks.finding.uncorrectable: {n} sectors hold data the disk could not recover. Keep a second copy and plan a replacement.
disks.finding.media: The drive failed to give data back {n} times. Keep a second copy and plan a replacement.
disks.finding.worn: The drive has used {n}% of the writes it is rated for. Plan a replacement.
disks.finding.hot: The disk is hot: {n} °C. Heat shortens its life — check the airflow around it.
disks.value.reallocatedHint: damaged and moved to the spare area
disks.value.uncorrectableHint: data the disk could not recover
disks.value.mediaHint: data the drive could not give back
disks.value.crcHint: a cable or a port, not the disk itself
disks.value.wearHint: of the writes the drive is rated for
disks.test.hint: The disk tests itself and stays usable meanwhile: a short test takes about two minutes, a long one reads the whole surface and takes hours.
error.disk.noSmart: This disk gives no SMART data, so it cannot test itself.
error.disk.testFailed: The disk refused to start the self-test.
attention.smart.failing.title: Disk {disk} reports that it is failing
attention.smart.failing.text: Copy what matters off it now and replace it.
attention.smart.critical.title: Disk {disk} raised a critical warning
attention.smart.critical.text: Copy what matters off it now and replace it.
attention.smart.spare.title: Disk {disk} is running out of spare blocks
